summary: Assess wheeling costs, contract terms, settlement and implementation risks. Explore the course outline and practical transaction exercises.
lede: Open-access electricity transaction training helps utility teams, generators and large buyers assess whether wheeling-based supply is commercially workable. Participants compare delivered-cost scenarios, review bilateral contract responsibilities and counterparty risks, and identify metering, settlement and network requirements to prepare a structured transaction decision brief.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who evaluate, negotiate or oversee electricity transactions that use network access and wheeling arrangements. It suits people with working familiarity in energy procurement, generation, utility operations, project development or electricity advisory work.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with electricity procurement, generation, utility operations, energy contracts or project development is recommended. No coding or electrical-engineering qualification is required; exercises focus on commercial analysis and Excel-based calculations.
